title: Promises and async/await
summary: Schedule work with setTimeout, chain promises with then and catch, write async/await code, and run tasks in parallel with Promise.all.
intro: Slow work like timers and network calls does not have to freeze your program. Node schedules the work, keeps running, and comes back when the result is ready. This lesson shows how to run code later, chain results with promises, write the same logic readably with `async` and `await`, and run several tasks at once.

steps.title: setTimeout and the event loop

example.title: Three timers
example.prompt: Read lines of `label delay`, schedule one timer per line, and watch synchronous code finish before any timer fires.
example.output:
start
scheduled 3 timers
fast after 10 ms
medium after 30 ms
slow after 50 ms
example.explanation: The loop only schedules the timers, so `start` and `scheduled 3 timers` print first: all synchronous code finishes before any callback runs. Then the timers fire by delay, not by input order: 10 ms, 30 ms, 50 ms. Each callback remembers its own `label` and `delay` because the loop declares them with `const`. Node exits after the 50 ms timer, the last one scheduled.

practice.title: Meal reminders
practice.prompt:
Schedule one reminder per input line and a final timer that runs after all of them.

1. The starter reads each line into `{ label, delay }` and prints `start` and `end`.
2. Between those two lines, schedule a timer for each task that prints its `label` after `delay` ms.
3. Schedule one more timer that prints `all done` 10 ms after the largest delay (`Math.max(...)` finds it).

Input:

```text
lunch 40
breakfast 10
dinner 70
```

Expected output:

```text
start
end
breakfast
lunch
dinner
all done
```

tests.output:
start
end
breakfast
lunch
dinner
all done

start
end
first
second
third
last
all done

hints: `end` prints before every label because the loop only schedules timers. The labels come later, ordered by delay.
Spread the delays into `Math.max`: map each task to its `delay` first.

steps.title: Promises with then, catch, and finally

example.title: Odd numbers fail
example.prompt: Send each input number through a delayed promise chain that rejects odd numbers, doubles, then adds 1.
example.output:
chains started
result: 9
cleanup
error: 7 is odd
cleanup
example.explanation: The loop builds both chains and moves on, so `chains started` prints first. The second chain waits 20 ms longer, so the two finish in input order. For 4, each `then` gets the value the previous one returned: 4, then 8, then 9. For 7, the first `then` throws, the remaining `then` calls are skipped, and `catch` prints the message. `finally` prints `cleanup` in both cases.

practice.title: Negative numbers fail
practice.prompt:
Send each input number through a delayed promise chain that rejects negative numbers, squares, then subtracts 1.

1. For each number `n` at index `i`, start with `delay(n, 20 * (i + 1))`.
2. In the first `then`, throw `new Error("negative input")` when the value is below 0, otherwise return it.
3. Add a `then` that squares the value and one that subtracts 1, then print `result: <value>`.
4. End the chain with `catch` printing `error: <message>` and `finally` printing `cleanup`.

Input:

```text
3 -2
```

Expected output:

```text
chains started
result: 8
cleanup
error: negative input
cleanup
```

tests.output:
chains started
result: 8
cleanup
error: negative input
cleanup

chains started
result: -1
cleanup
result: 24
cleanup
error: negative input
cleanup

chains started
error: negative input
cleanup

hints: Copy the shape of the example chain and change the check and the two math steps.
0 is not negative, so it goes through: 0 squared is 0, minus 1 is -1.

steps.title: async and await

example.title: Install steps
example.prompt: Read steps as `name ms`, run them one after another with `await`, and skip any step slower than 100 ms instead of crashing.
example.output:
connect done
download skipped (too slow)
verify done
all steps finished
example.explanation: `runStep` is async, so its `throw` becomes a rejected promise rather than a crash. `safeStep` uses `return await`, which makes the rejection happen inside its `try`, so its own `catch` turns it into a `skipped` line. In `main`, `await` inside `for...of` finishes each step before starting the next, so lines print in input order even though `verify` is faster than `connect`.

practice.title: Task runner
practice.prompt:
Run tasks in input order with async/await and report each one as ok or failed.

1. In `runTask`, await `sleep(ms)`, then throw `new Error("task failed")` when `name` is `fail`, otherwise return `<name> ok`.
2. In `safeTask`, `return await runTask(name, ms)` inside `try` and return `<name> error (<message>)` from `catch`.
3. In `main`, loop over `tasks` with `for...of`, await `safeTask` for each, and print what it returns before the final line.

Input:

```text
load 30
fail 10
save 20
```

Expected output:

```text
load ok
fail error (task failed)
save ok
all tasks finished
```

tests.output:
load ok
fail error (task failed)
save ok
all tasks finished

ping ok
pong ok
all tasks finished

fail error (task failed)
retry ok
fail error (task failed)
all tasks finished

hints: Each task must finish before the next starts, so `fail 10` still prints after `load 30`.
Without `await` after `return`, the rejection skips `safeTask`'s `catch` and crashes the program.

steps.title: Running promises together

example.title: Health check
example.prompt: Read services as `name ms up` or `name ms down`, check them in parallel, and compare what `allSettled`, `all`, and `race` report.
example.stdin:
db 30 up
cache 10 up
api 20 down
example.output:
db: up (30 ms)
cache: up (10 ms)
api: down (api timed out)
all: failed (api timed out)
first: cache
example.explanation: `map` starts all three checks at once, so the `allSettled` round takes about 30 ms, not 60. `allSettled` waits for all of them and keeps input order, so `db` prints first even though `cache` finished first. `Promise.all` rejects at 20 ms with the first error, `api timed out`. Had every service been up, it would print the names in input order. `Promise.race` settles with `cache`, the first to finish. It still sits in `try`, because a fastest service that is down makes the race reject.

practice.title: Status page
practice.prompt:
Check every service in parallel and summarize the results with allSettled, all, and race.

1. Run `Promise.allSettled` over all checks and print `<name>: up` or `<name>: down (<reason message>)` for each service, in input order.
2. Print `up: <count>`, the number of fulfilled results.
3. Run `Promise.all` over fresh checks and print `all: ok (<names>)` with the names in input order joined by `, `, or `all: failed (<message>)` when it rejects.
4. Run `Promise.race` over fresh checks and print `first: <name>`, or `first: failed (<message>)` when the fastest service is down.

Input:

```text
web 20 up
mail 40 down
dns 10 up
```

Expected output:

```text
web: up
mail: down (mail timed out)
dns: up
up: 2
all: failed (mail timed out)
first: dns
```

tests.stdin:
web 20 up
mail 40 down
dns 10 up
tests.output:
web: up
mail: down (mail timed out)
dns: up
up: 2
all: failed (mail timed out)
first: dns

auth: up
queue: up
up: 2
all: ok (auth, queue)
first: queue

search: down (search timed out)
logs: up
up: 1
all: failed (search timed out)
first: failed (search timed out)

hints: `services.map((service) => check(service))` starts every check at once. Call it again for each of the three combinators.
Each result lines up with the service at the same index. A rejected one has `reason`, an `Error` with a `message`.
Wrap both `Promise.all` and `Promise.race` in `try`/`catch`, since either can reject.

recap:
- `setTimeout(callback, ms)` runs a callback later. All synchronous code finishes first, timers fire in order of delay, and Node exits after the last callback.
- `new Promise((resolve, reject) => ...)` wraps work that finishes later.
- Each `then` gets what the previous one returned. A throw jumps to the next `catch`, and `finally` runs either way.
- An `async` function returns a promise. `await` pauses it until a promise settles, and `try`/`catch` handles rejections.
- No top-level `await` in CommonJS: write `async function main()` and call `main();`.
- Inside `try`, write `return await promise` so the local `catch` sees the rejection.
- `sleep(ms)` is `new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms))`.
- `await` in `for...of` runs tasks in sequence. `forEach` does not wait.
- `Promise.all(items.map(async (item) => ...))` runs tasks in parallel, resolves to results in input order, and rejects on the first failure.
- `Promise.allSettled` reports every `status` with its `value` or `reason`. `Promise.race` settles like the fastest promise.
- Catch every rejection, because an unhandled one crashes Node.
